label: Part identifier
partDesc: The unique identify of any entity within the dictionary.
partInstr: Every entity in the ODM has a partID. The partID must be unique with no duplcates. partIDs are short. partIDs that are constructed by different part attributes can be up 28 characters (check max), but each part attibute should be 1 to 5 characters. partIDs are machine readible, but a knowledgable user can understand what they represent. partID are used, for example, as a header in an Excel input table. Numbers are allowed but there no other special characters other than `_`. `_` is a reserved character that is used to generate a partID using a compoent or table attributes. A partID for a subComponent is automatically generated using attributes of a component. For example, the partID for the compoent `SARS-CoV-2` is `covid`. `Covid` can have many subComponents including different groups (Covid-19-al, Covid-19-va, ovid-pr (allele, variant or protein) or units and aggregatrions (i.e. covid-al-N1-mean-cpl representing ovid allele N1, mean observation of viral copies per litre of effluent). A similar approach to naming subComponent is use for naming parts in a reprotTable.

label: Collection period and number
partDesc: Composite collection number.period.
partInstr:
This a composite measure that combines `collection period` (collPer) and `collection number` (collNum). Collection number and period can be used to reduce the number of table headings during data collection. In data storage, `collNum` and `collPeriod` should be transformed to `collPer` and `collNum`. For Grab sample, Surface swab, or Area proportional sample just enter 1

In case of Composite, Flow-proportional collection, the number of subsamples followed by a dot, followed by the period of the sampling, in hours.
For example, for 4 composite subsamples covering a 8 hours period, the entry would be 4.2
For time-proportional 24 subsamples collected every hour, the entry would be 24.1
For volume-proportional, the entry for 24 subsamples collected over 24 hours should be 24.24, in this case the period part of the entry should be understood as the total collection time instead of the periodicity of the collection.

For a COSCA ball or Moore swab collecting for 24 hours, the entry would be 1.24

label: Last edited
partDesc: The date the entry was last updated.
partInstr: Use lastEdited if an entry is updated. Leave lastEdited blank or 'NA' for the first entry. Updates can include additions or revisions of the entry for any reason. For example, a wastewater measure was repeated later with an improved method. You can revise the entry by updating the value and then adding the date the new measure was performed to 'lastEdited'.  To ensure data provenance, the best practice in this example is to generate a new entry with the same measureID as the original measureID. The original and new measures are kept in the database with a date in the 'lastEdited' field for the new entry but not the original one. Some databases may choose a delete-and-replace approach where the original entry is deleted and replaced by a new entry. In this approach, the 'lastEdited' field indicates the delete and replace occurred.

label: Andes virus (ANDV) hantavirus
partDesc: Andes virus (ANDV) is the most common cause of hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) in South America. Andes virus is transmitted mainly by the long-tailed pygmy rice rat. Orthohantavirus andesense.

label: Ebola virus, Orthoebolavirus zairense
partDesc: Orthoebolavirus zairense or Zaire ebolavirus, more commonly known as Ebola virus, is one of six known species within the genus Ebolavirus. Four of the six known ebolaviruses, including EBOV, cause a severe and often fatal hemorrhagic fever in humans and other mammals, known as Ebola virus disease (EVD).

label: Sudan virus, Orthoebolavirus sudanense
partDesc: Sudan virus (species Orthoebolavirus sudanense) causes Sudan virus disease.

label: Taï Forest virus, Orthoebolavirus taiense
partDesc: Orthoebolavirus taiense (formerly Taï Forest ebolavirus) is a rare viral species that causes Taï Forest virus disease in humans. It is one of four orthoebolaviruses known to cause illness in people, with only one confirmed human infection ever recorded.

label: Bundibugyo virus, Orthoebolavirus bundibugyoense
partDesc: The species Bundibugyo ebolavirus is the taxonomic home of one virus, Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), that forms filamentous virions and is closely related to the Zaire ebolaviruses (EBOV). The virus is one of several that can cause Ebola disease in humans, taking the form of viral hemorrhagic fever.

label: Ebola Virus Disease (EVD)
partDesc: Ebola, also known as Ebola virus disease (EVD) and Ebola hemorrhagic fever (EHF), is a zoonotic viral hemorrhagic fever in humans and other primates, caused by four of the six known ebolaviruses.

label: Orthohantavirus Group
partDesc: A group of measures/methods related to Orthohantaviruses.
partInstr: Used to describe the organism information for general measures.

label: Hantavirus hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS)
partDesc: Hantavirus hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is a hemorrhagic fever caused by hantavirus infection. Symptoms usually occur 2 weeks after exposure to the hantavirus and come in five distinct clinical stages: febrile (toxic), hypotensive, low urine production (oliguric), high urine production (diuretic), and recovery.

label: Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS)
partDesc: Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS), also called hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), is a severe respiratory disease caused by hantavirus infection. The main features of illness are microvascular leakage and acute respiratory distress syndrome. Symptoms occur anywhere from one to eight weeks after exposure to the virus and come in three distinct phases.

label: Sin Nombre virus (SNV) hantavirus
partDesc: Sin Nombre virus (SNV) is the most common cause of hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) in North America. Sin Nombre virus is transmitted mainly by the western deer mouse (Peromyscus sonoriensis).

label: Hantaan virus (HTNV) hantavirus
partDesc: Hantaan virus (HTNV) is the main cause of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in East Asia. Hantaan virus is transmitted by the striped field mouse (Apodemus agrarius).

label: Seoul virus (SEOV) hantavirus
partDesc: Seoul virus (SEOV) is one of the main causes of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS). Seoul virus is transmitted by the brown rat (Rattus norvegicus) and the black rat (Rattus rattus).

label: Puumala virus (PUUV) hantavirus
partDesc: Puumala virus (PUUV) is the main cause of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in Europe and Russia. Puumala virus is transmitted by the bank vole (Clethrionomys glareolus).

label: Dobrava-Belgrade virus (DOBV) hantavirus
partDesc: Dobrava-Belgrade virus (DOBV) is the main cause of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in southern Europe.

partInstr: If a column doesn’t have tag value at the end, then it means it applies to all groups, while one with a tag only applie to fields with the same tag value. For example, a value under qr_qualityFlag (with no tag) applies to fields in the group with tag == .odm10 and all other groups. If there’s a column called qr_qualityFlag.odm10, however, then the group with that .odm10 tag uses the value from qr_qualityFlag.odm10 instead of from qr_qualityFlag (like wat_sa_nr_hMe_hUn_hAg_NR_value.odm10 and mr_unit.odm10, for example).

partDesc: Measures of Aichivirus A, the species of aichivirus in the Kobuvirus genus, and picornavirus family. Typically a cause of gastrorenteritis in human or animal hosts.

label: Aichivirus B (Bovine kobuvirus)
partDesc: Measures of Aichivirus B, the species of aichivirus in the Kobuvirus genus, and picornavirus family. Typically a cause of gastrorenteritis in human or animal hosts. Also called Bovine kobuvirus.

label: Aichivirus C (Porcine kobuviru)
partDesc: Measures of Aichivirus C, the species of aichivirus in the Kobuvirus genus, and picornavirus family. Typically a cause of gastrorenteritis in human or animal hosts. Also called Porcine kobuvirus.

label: Aichivirus D (kagovirus from black cattles)
partDesc: Measures of Aichivirus D, the species of aichivirus in the Kobuvirus genus, and picornavirus family. Typically a cause of gastrorenteritis in human or animal hosts. Also called kagovirus from black cattle.

label: Aichivirus E (Rabbit picornavirus)
partDesc: Measures of Aichivirus E, the species of aichivirus in the Kobuvirus genus, and picornavirus family. Typically a cause of gastrorenteritis in human or animal hosts. Also called Rabbit picornavirus.

label: Aichivirus F (Bat kobuvirus)
partDesc: Measures of Aichivirus F, the species of aichivirus in the Kobuvirus genus, and picornavirus family. Typically a cause of gastrorenteritis in human or animal hosts. Also called bat kobuvirus.

label: Human Aichi virus (AiV)
partDesc: Viral strain of Aichivirus A known to infect humans, typically of three known genotypes: A, B, or C.

partDesc: A gene target for aichivirus, it is the genomic segment that encodes the structural viral capsid proteins forming the outer shell of the Aichivirus.

label: Bocaparvovirus
partDesc: Bocaparvovirus is a genus of viruses in the subfamily Parvovirinae of the virus family Parvoviridae. Humans, cattle, and dogs serve as natural hosts. There are 36 species in this genus. Diseases associated with this genus include, in humans, acute respiratory illness, and in cattle, diarrhea and mild respiratory symptoms.

label: Human bocavirus (HBoV)
partDesc: Human bocavirus (HBoV) is the name given to all viruses in the genus Bocaparvovirus of virus family Parvoviridae that are known to infect humans. Some of these viruses cause human disease. HBoV1 is strongly implicated in causing some cases of lower respiratory tract infection, especially in young children, and several of the viruses have been linked to gastroenteritis, although the full clinical role of this emerging infectious disease remains to be elucidated.

label: Cacipacore virus (Orthoflavivirus cacipacoreense)
partDesc: Orthoflavivirus cacipacoreense, causitive agent of the rare Cacipacore virus

partInstr: Used to describe the organism information for general measures.

label: Porcine Circovirus 1 (PCV-1)
partDesc: Porcine Circoviruses (PCV) are the smallest viruses replicating autonomously in eukaryotic cells. The virions are non-enveloped and spherical with a diameter of 16-18 nm and the covalently closed and single-stranded DNA genomes comprise less than 1800 nucleotides. Porcine circovirus type 1 (PCV1) is not linked with a disease.

label: Porcine Circovirus 2 (PCV-2)
partDesc: Porcine Circoviruses (PCV) are the smallest viruses replicating autonomously in eukaryotic cells. The virions are non-enveloped and spherical with a diameter of 16-18 nm and the covalently closed and single-stranded DNA genomes comprise less than 1800 nucleotides. Porcine circovirus type 2 (PCV2) is the etiological agent of Postweaning Multisystemic Wasting Syndrome (PMWS), a new emerging and multifactorial disease in swine.

label: Cosavirus Group
partDesc: A group of measures/methods related to cosaviruses.
partInstr: Used to describe the organism information for general measures.

label: Cosavirus (CosaV)
partDesc: Cosavirus is a genus of viruses in the order Picornavirales, in the family Picornaviridae. Human serve as natural hosts. There are 5 species od enteric viruses in this genus.

label: Deltaretrovirus Group
partDesc: A group of measures/methods related to deltaretroviruses.
partInstr: Used to describe the organism information for general measures.

label: Deltaretrovirus
partDesc: Deltaretrovirus is a genus of the Retroviridae family. It consists of exogenous horizontally transmitted viruses found in several groups of mammals. This genus of viruses is known for its propensity to target immune cells and oncogenicity. Infection is usually asymptomatic, but inflammation and cancer can develop over time.

label: Primate T-lymphotropic virus 1
partDesc: Human T-cell lymphotropic virus type 1, Primate T-lymphotropic virus 1, or human T-lymphotropic virus (HTLV-I or HTLV-1), also called the adult T-cell lymphoma virus type 1, is a deltaretrovirus of the human T-lymphotropic virus (HTLV) family. Latin species name: Deltaretrovirus priTlym1.

label: Primate T-lymphotropic virus 2
partDesc: Human T-cell lymphotropic virus 2, or Primate T-lymphotropic virus 2 (HTLV-II or HTLV-2), is a deltaretrovirus of the human T-lymphotropic virus (HTLV) family. Latin species name: Deltaretrovirus priTlym2.

label: Eastern equine encephalitis virus (EEEV)
partDesc: Eastern equine encephalitis virus (EEEV) is defined as a neurotropic alphavirus that causes severe disease in horses, characterized by high mortality rates and pathological lesions in the central nervous system, including inflammation and infiltration of immune cells.

label: Eastern equine encephalitis virus group
partDesc: A group of measures/methods related to eastern equine encephalitis viruses.
partInstr: Used to describe the organism information for general measures.

label: Erythroparvovirus Group
partDesc: A group of measures/methods related to erythroparvoviruses.
partInstr: Used to describe the organism information for general measures.

label: Erythroparvovirus
partDesc: Erythroparvovirus is defined as a small DNA virus that belongs to the Parvoviridae family, known for causing various illnesses, including fifth disease, arthritis, and anemia, particularly in immunocompromised individuals.

label: human parvovirus B19 (B19V)
partDesc: Human parvovirus B19 is defined as a nonenveloped, single-stranded DNA virus belonging to the Erythrovirus genus of the Parvoviridae family, which primarily infects humans and can cause a variety of syndromes, including erythema infectiosum, arthropathy, and complications such as aplastic anemia and fetal hydrops.

label: Giardia Group
partDesc: A group of measures/methods related to Giardia.
partInstr: Used to describe the organism information for general measures.

label: Giardia duodenalis
partDesc: A protozoan parasite that causes anthroponotic or zoonotic diarrheal disease which can be opportunistic or affect healthy, immunocompetent individuals. Giardia duodenalis is the one commonly described type of Giardia, that is found in mammals including humans. This species complex comprise eight assemblages

label: Giardia 18S rRNA
partDesc: The 18S ribosomal RNA (18S rRNA) gene in Giardia is a primary genetic target used for detecting, identifying, and classifying the microscopic intestinal parasite responsible for giardiasis.

label: Gammaretrovirus Group
partDesc: A group of measures/methods related to gammaretroviruses.
partInstr: Used to describe the organism information for general measures.

label: Gammaretrovirus
partDesc: Gammaretrovirus is a genus in the Retroviridae family. Example species are the murine leukemia virus and the feline leukemia virus. They cause various sarcomas, leukemias and immune deficiencies in mammals, reptiles and birds.

label: Lymphocryptovirus Group
partDesc: A group of measures/methods related to lymphocryptoviruses.
partInstr: Used to describe the organism information for general measures.

label: Lymphocryptovirus
partDesc: Lymphocryptovirus is a genus of viruses in the order Herpesvirales, in the family Orthoherpesviridae, in the subfamily Gammaherpesvirinae. This genus includes the human-infecting Epstein–Barr virus, as well as viruses that infect both Old World monkeys and New World monkeys. Also called gamma-1 herpesviruses, there are nine species in this genus. Diseases associated with this genus include: mononucleosis, Burkitt's lymphoma, and nasopharyngeal carcinoma.

label: Human mastadenovirus Group
partDesc: A group of measures/methods related to human mastadenoviruses.
partInstr: Used to describe the organism information for general measures.

label: Human mastadenoviruses (HAdVs)
partDesc: Human mastadenoviruses (HAdVs) are non-enveloped, double-stranded icosahedral DNA viruses, approximately 90–100 nm in diameter, with fibre projections on each of the 12 vertices. The genome is approximately 30–35 kilobases in length and encodes more than 30 structural and non-structural proteins. HAdV belongs to the genus Mastadenovirus, one of five genera within the Adenoviridae family. Within Mastadenovirus, seven known groups have been identified (A-G), which can be further classified into 54 serotypes.

label: Human mastadenovirus genotype group A
partDesc: Group A of the human mastadenovirus genus (HAdV-A). Includes serotypes 12, 18, and 31.

label: Human mastadenovirus genotype group B
partDesc: Group B of the human mastadenovirus genus (HAdV-B). Includes serotypes 3, and 16.

label: Human mastadenovirus genotype group C
partDesc: Group C of the human mastadenovirus genus (HAdV-C). Includes serotypes 1, 2, 5, and  6.

label: Human mastadenovirus genotype group D
partDesc: Group D of the human mastadenovirus genus (HAdV-D). Includes serotypes 8, 17, 19, 23, 36, 51, and 58.

label: Human mastadenovirus genotype group E
partDesc: Group E of the human mastadenovirus genus (HAdV-E). Includes serotype 4.

label: Human mastadenovirus genotype group F
partDesc: Group F of the human mastadenovirus genus (HAdV-F). Includes serotypes 40 and 41.

label: Parechovirus group
partDesc: A group of measures/methods related to parechoviruses.
partInstr: Used to describe the organism information for general measures.

label: Human Parechovirus (PeV)
partDesc: Human parechovirus (HPeV; family Picornaviridae, genus Parechovirus) is a nonenveloped virus with a positive-sense single-stranded RNA genome that infects humans. HPeV strains are currently subdivided into 16 genotypes (i.e., HPeV1 to HPeV16), and HPeV1 and HPeV3 are the genotypes mostly causing gastroenteritis, respiratory syndrome, and febrile illness mainly in young children.

label: Human Parechovirus-1 (HPeV1)
partDesc: Human parechovirus (HPeV) of the genotype 1 (HPeV1), capable of causing gastroenteritis, respiratory syndrome, and febrile illness in humans.

label: Picobirnavirus Group
partDesc: A group of measures/methods related to picobirnaviruses.
partInstr: Used to describe the organism information for general measures.

label: Picobirnavirus
partDesc: The single genus of the Picobirnaviridae family, Picobirnavirus, members of which have been identified in the feces of humans, rabbits, and a variety of other species of mammals, reptiles, and birds. Picobirnaviruses have been increasingly recognized with the advent of deep sequencing analysis of fecal specimens from many species of animals, and distinct genetic subgroups are now described.

label: Polyomavirus Group
partDesc: A group of measures/methods related to polyomaviruses.
partInstr: Used to describe the organism information for general measures.

label: Human Polyomavirus (PyV)
partDesc: Studies reported human Polyomaviruses (PyV) (mainly strains BK and JC) contaminating water and food. These strains are, respectively, associated with nephropathy and progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy. Others link them to common respiratory illnesses.

label: JC Polyomavirus (JCV)
partDesc: JCPyV, or human polyomavirus JC, is defined a polyomavirus and an etiological agent associated with progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy, characterized by demyelination in the central nervous system, and has been detected in certain tumors, suggesting a potential but unproven link to cancer development.

label: BK Polyomavirus (BKV)
partDesc: BKPyV, or human polyomavirus BK, is defined a polyomavirus and an etiological agent associated with nephropathy.

label: Roseolovirus (Human Herpesvirus-6) Group
partDesc: A group of measures/methods related to roseoloviruses.
partInstr: Used to describe the organism information for general measures.

label: Roseolovirus (Human Herpesvirus-6)
partDesc: Roseolovirus refers to a group of viruses, including HHV-6A and HHV-6B, that are characterized by their ability to cause various diseases, persist in latency within different cell types, and integrate into the human genome. Their detection does not necessarily indicate causation of disease, highlighting the need for careful interpretation of diagnostic results within clinical contexts.

label: Human Herpesvirus-6A (HHV-6A)
partDesc: HHV-6A is a roseolovirus that has been described as more neurovirulent, and as such is more frequently found in patients with neuroinflammatory diseases such as multiple sclerosis.

label: Human Herpesvirus-6B (HHV-6B)
partDesc: HHV-6B is a roseolovirus and the cause of the common childhood illness exanthema subitum (also known as roseola infantum or sixth disease). It is passed on from child to child. It is uncommon for adults to contract this disease as most people have had it by kindergarten, and once contracted, immunity arises and prevents future reinfection. Additionally, HHV-6B reactivation is common in transplant recipients, which can cause several clinical manifestations such as encephalitis, bone marrow suppression, and pneumonitis.

label: Salivirus Group
partDesc: A group of measures/methods related to salivirus.
partInstr: Used to describe the organism information for general measures.

label: Salivirus A (Salivirus aklasse)
partDesc: Salivirus A (Salivirus aklasse) has been identified in humans and chimpanzees and may cause acute gastroenteritis in humans, having been detected in 0% to 8.7% of fecal samples collected from gastroenteritis in different human populations. Salivirus is ubiquitous in wastewater of human origin and river water specimens worldwide and represents a potential indicator human RNA virus for monitoring of environmental samples.

label: Saffold virus (SAFV)
partDesc: Saffold virus (SAFV) is an emerging human cardiovirus associated with respiratory and gastrointestinal infection, and, more recently, to symptoms related to the endocrine, cardiovascular, and neurological systems.

label: Tanapox
partDesc: Tanapox (a virus from the genus Yatapoxvirus) was first seen among individuals in the flood plain of the Tana River in Kenya during two epidemics (1957 and 1962) of acute febrile illness accompanied by localized skin lesions.

label: Torque Teno Virus Group

partInstr: Used to describe the organism information for general measures.

label: Torque Teno Virus
partDesc: Torque teno virus (TTV) is the type species in the genus Anellovirus. The viruses are small (30–50 nm) and non-enveloped with a circular single-stranded DNA genome that is approximately 3.8 kb in size. More than 90% of adults worldwide are said to be infected with TTV. The viruses have not been conclusively shown to cause disease in humans, although they have been associated with some acute respiratory illnesses in infants.

label: Human Parechovirus-3 (HPeV3)
partDesc: Human parechovirus (HPeV) of the genotype 3 (HPeV3), capable of causing gastroenteritis, respiratory syndrome, and febrile illness in humans.
